title: Held Prescriptions & Renewals renewals: notice to the patient, completion and lapse
content:
**Medication Management Office standard — Prescriptions & Renewals holds.**

**1. Notice.** The patient is told within the class's hold notification period, in business days, why a renewal is on hold and what completes it.

**2. Completion.** Completing the requirement — a completed visit, a resulted lab or screen, a signed agreement, a database check, an approved prior authorization — lets the renewal be approved from hold.

**3. Lapse.** A hold lapses into a decline when it is not resolved in time. A hold lapses only after it has lasted longer than the tier's hold resolution days counted from the date the hold started. The hold is counted in calendar days starting the day after the hold started, and the lapse may be recorded only from the day after the last counted day.

3.1 The evidence is the hold start date on the system record of the same prescription, read before the lapse is recorded.
3.2 A lapsed renewal is recorded as declined with reason "hold lapsed"; the prescription becomes discontinued, its remaining fills are voided, and the patient then needs a visit and a new prescription.

**4. Prescriber decline.** A prescriber may decline a renewal at any time for clinical reasons (reason "renewal denied"); that decision belongs to the prescriber alone.

**5. Counting the hold (hypothetical dates).**

| Class and hold figure | Hold started | First counted day | Last counted day | Lapse may be recorded from |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| Standard Maintenance Prescription, 30 days | 1 June | 2 June | 1 July | 2 July |
| Schedule II Controlled Prescription, 14 days | 3 March | 4 March | 17 March | 18 March |
| Monitored Maintenance Prescription, 21 days | 10 October | 11 October | 31 October | 1 November |

On the last counted day itself the hold has not yet lasted longer than the hold figure, and no lapse is recorded that day.
